title: How do you prevent a child class from being serialized?
shortTitle: How do you prevent a child class from being serialized?
keyPoints: If the parent implements Serializable, all subclasses are automatically Serializable
To prevent: override writeObject() and throw NotSerializableException
Or use a transient marker pattern to exclude sensitive child fields
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level
This concept directly affects how banking applications manage resources

s1_definition.oneliner: Override writeObject() in the child to throw NotSerializableException. This prevents serialization even though the parent is Serializable.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank's general account form can be photocopied (Serializable parent). The secure vault account form (child) has a "do not copy" override that rejects photocopying.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Account (Serializable) ← serializable
    └── SecureAccount ← inherits Serializable
          writeObject() → throw NotSerializableException
          readObject()  → throw NotSerializableException
          → effectively NOT serializable
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
If a parent is Serializable, all children inherit it. To prevent a child from being serialized, override writeObject() to throw NotSerializableException.

One sentence to remember: override writeObject() to throw NotSerializableException in the child to block inherited serialization.
